questions.question: ______ was one of the first Indian rulers to lead an armed rebellion against the British East India Company in 1824 against the implementation of the Doctrine of Lapse.
questions.solution:
Kittur Chennamma, the Queen of Kittur (Karnataka), led an armed rebellion in 1824.
  • She fought against the British policy of Doctrine of Lapse long before the 1857 revolt.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers founded an educational institution, Hindu Widows Home, in Poona in the year 1896?
questions.solution:
Dhondo Keshav Karve (Maharishi Karve) founded the Hindu Widows Home in Poona in 1896.
  • He was a pioneer in women's education and social reform.
  • He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1958.

questions.question: In which of the following states is Bishnupur, famous for terracotta temples, located?
questions.solution:
Bishnupur, famous for its 17th-century terracotta temples, is located in West Bengal.
  • It was the capital of the Malla Kings.
  • The temples are dedicated to Lord Krishna (Radha-Krishna).

questions.question: The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
questions.solution:
The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dacca (now Dhaka).
  • Key founders included Aga Khan III and Nawab Salimullah.

questions.question: Who among the following was elected as the President of the Indian National Congress in the year 1938 and 1939?
questions.solution:
Subhash Chandra Bose was elected President of the INC at the Haripura Session (1938) and the Tripuri Session (1939).
  • He later resigned due to differences with Gandhi and formed the Forward Bloc.

questions.question: Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya is credited with popularising the slogan '______'.
questions.solution:
Madan Mohan Malviya popularized the slogan 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs).
  • The slogan is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.
  • He founded the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916.

questions.question: The Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in 1920 by Baba Ramchandra and Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • It was formed to organize peasants against high rents and evictions by landlords (talukdars).

questions.question: ______ succumbed to injuries inflicted on him during a peaceful demonstration against the Simon Commission.
questions.solution:
Lala Lajpat Rai, known as 'Punjab Kesari', died in 1928 due to a lathi charge.
  • He was protesting against the Simon Commission.
  • His death was avenged by Bhagat Singh and his comrades.

questions.question: Gandhiji delivered the famous 'Do or Die' speech on ______.
questions.solution:
Gandhiji gave the 'Do or Die' speech on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay.
  • This launched the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Janapada Geete, which includes the vachanas of Basavanna, is associated with the state of ______.
questions.solution:
Janapada Geete and the vachanas of Basavanna are cultural heritages of Karnataka.
  • Basavanna was a 12th-century philosopher and the founder of Lingayatism.

questions.question: Which Prime Minister among the following had signed the Assam Accord with the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad in 1985?
questions.solution:
Rajiv Gandhi signed the Assam Accord in 1985 to end the 6-year-long anti-foreigner agitation in Assam.
  • The agreement was between the Govt of India and the All Assam Students Union (AASU).

questions.question: Whose proclamation of November 1, 1858 declared that thereafter India would be governed by and in the name of the British Monarch through a Secretary of State?
questions.solution:
Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858 ended the East India Company's rule.
  • India came under the direct rule of the British Crown.
  • The Governor-General was given the title of Viceroy.

questions.question: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 between Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori.
  • Prithviraj Chauhan won the first battle, but lost the second in 1192.

questions.question: In which year did the Sepoy Mutiny end?
questions.solution:
The Sepoy Mutiny (Great Revolt of 1857) officially ended in 1858.
  • It led to the Government of India Act 1858.

questions.question: Which of the following cities became the capital of Bahamani sultanate immediately after its foundation?
questions.solution:
Ahsanabad (Gulbarga) was the first capital of the Bahamani Sultanate, founded by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah in 1347.
  • The capital was later shifted to Bidar in 1425.

questions.question: Which of the following Gupta rulers married a girl from the Licchavi dynasty?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi, a princess of the Licchavi clan.
  • This alliance strengthened the Gupta Empire's prestige and power.
  • He was the first Gupta ruler to take the title Maharajadhiraja.

questions.question: Who among the following nationalist leaders was popularly known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.solution:
Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) was known as 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Nation).
  • He was the co-founder of the Swaraj Party in 1923 along with Motilal Nehru.

questions.question: Who was the last king of the Mauryan dynasty?
questions.solution:
Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan Dynasty.
  • He was assassinated by his commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga, who founded the Shunga Dynasty in 185 B.C.

questions.question: In the Mughal provincial administration, broadly speaking, Diwani meant:
questions.option_2: administration of law and order and criminal justice
questions.solution:
In Mughal administration, Diwani referred to revenue and civil justice administration.
  • The Nizamat referred to military and police functions.

questions.question: Who assassinated Michael O’Dwyer, the British official responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
Udham Singh assassinated Michael O’Dwyer in London in 1940.
  • O’Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab during the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.question: Who among the following built the first European fort in India in the year 1503?
questions.solution:
The Portuguese built the first European fort in India (Fort Emmanuel) at Kochi in 1503.
  • Afonso de Albuquerque was instrumental in establishing Portuguese power in India.

questions.question: The Chalukya Dynasty ruled in Vatapi which is in the modern day Indian state of ______.
questions.solution:
The Chalukya Dynasty ruled from Vatapi (modern-day Badami) in Karnataka.
  • Pulakeshin II was the most famous ruler of this dynasty.

questions.question: In 1526, ______ defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat and captured Delhi and Agra.
questions.solution:
In 1526, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat.
  • This marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Military commanders in Akbar’s empire were called ‘______’.
questions.solution:
In Akbar’s empire, military commanders were known as Faujdars.
  • Bakhshis were the paymasters, and Kotwals were the town police commanders.

questions.question: Murshid Quli Khan was the Nawab of ______.
questions.solution:
Murshid Quli Khan was the first Nawab of Bengal (1717).
  • He shifted the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad.
